verdict: Zebra's sales jumped 22% to a record $1.6B as the Elo Touch acquisition and double-digit organic growth in both segments outweighed pricier memory chips that squeezed gross margin from 48.0% to 45.7%.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +22% vs a year ago; organic growth was +11%

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: profit before interest, tax and write-downs, on Zebra's adjusted basis

segments.name: Connected Frontline
segments.note: Mobile computers, barcode scanners and printers used by frontline workers — Zebra's larger segment, renamed from Enterprise Visibility & Mobility. Reported sales rose 35%, helped by the Elo Touch acquisition; organic growth was 15%.

segments.name: Asset Visibility & Automation
segments.note: RFID readers, machine-vision and automation products that track goods and assets — renamed from Asset Intelligence & Tracking. Reported sales rose 8%; organic growth was 7%.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and marketing ($183M) plus general and administrative costs ($122M) — the people who sell and run the business.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new scanners, mobile computers, RFID and automation products.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down technology and customer relationships bought in acquisitions — up from $25M a year ago after the Elo Touch deal.

opex.name: Acquisition and integration costs
opex.note: Costs of buying and absorbing Elo Touch and other acquisitions — down from $10M a year ago.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $35M, a $3M foreign-exchange loss and $1M of other expense — a net $39M cost below operating income.
oneTimers: The Elo Touch acquisition lifted reported growth well above the 11.3% organic rate and pushed intangible amortization up to $37M from $25M a year ago; acquisition and integration costs themselves were just $1M this quarter (vs $10M a year ago).
Exit and restructuring costs printed at $0 in the quarter, so no line is shown for them.

takeaways.title: A record quarter, half of it bought
takeaways.text: Sales hit a record $1,614M, up 22%. Organic growth — excluding acquisitions and currency — was 11.3%, with Connected Frontline up 15% organically and Asset Visibility & Automation up 7%.

takeaways.title: Memory chips squeezed margins
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell to 45.7% from 48.0% a year ago, mainly because memory components cost more and the product mix shifted, partly offset by pricing actions and currency.

takeaways.title: Profit grew faster than sales
takeaways.text: Non-GAAP EPS rose 28% to $4.95 and GAAP EPS rose to $3.43 from $1.97. Zebra raised its full-year outlook and has repurchased over $640M of shares in the first nine months.

footerNote: Zebra's fiscal third quarter ended October 3, 2026. Cost of sales combines the printed tangible-products cost ($745M) and services and software cost ($131M); SG&A combines the printed selling and marketing ($183M) and general and administrative ($122M) lines. Segment names are the ones Zebra prints now — Connected Frontline and Asset Visibility & Automation.
